profile.bio: I am a Computer Science Ph.D. researcher and the founding doctoral student in Dr. Tasnuva Farheen's group at Louisiana State University, recipient of the 2026 Quantum Rising Star Award at Rice University (QS3). My research focuses primarily on Quantum Hardware Security and Quantum Communication. My work also extends to quantum characterization, verification, and validation (QCVV) and the analysis of non-classical correlations from an information-theoretic perspective.

pillars.title: Quantum Hardware Security, Pulse Control & QCVV
pillars.funding: Louisiana Board of Regents (BoR, Proposal no. 033A-26)
pillars.summary: Investigating how adversarial pulses exploit interqubit coupling to induce logical errors in shared superconducting quantum processors. My work combines pulse-level simulation, quantum process tomography, and isometry-based circuit extraction to reconstruct induced error channels and characterize an asymmetric crosstalk attack mechanism. I also develop methods for quantum characterization, verification, and validation (QCVV) using residual Pauli transfer matrices, including calibrated detection of weak coherent two-qubit crosstalk versus local calibration drift at matched average gate infidelity.
highlights: Pulse-level simulation of crosstalk attacks and pulse-to-circuit characterization of their induced error channels [C4, C5].
Multiqubit pulse calibration, including Rabi calibration and echoed cross-resonance gates, alongside open-system dynamics and process characterization.
Published at IEEE QCE 2025 [C4] and ACM QSec 2025 [C5]; accepted at IEEE HOST 2027 [C7].

pillars.title: Quantum Communication, Correlations & Error Correction
pillars.summary: Developing quantum communication protocols using entanglement, quantum error correction, and information-theoretic measures of quantum correlations. My work includes improving the fidelity of encoded Bell pairs, designing an adaptive superdense-coding testbed, and probabilistic teleportation of repetition-encoded logical states through partially entangled GHZ channels using optimal positive operator-valued measurements (POVMs). Current research investigates how quantum discord and entanglement of formation can guide pair-preserving recovery and message decoding when joint operations on the received qubit pair are available.
highlights: Error correction for encoded Bell pairs [J1], adaptive superdense coding [C6], and POVM-based teleportation of encoded logical states [J4].
Published in Heliyon 2023 [J1, first author], AVS Quantum Science 2025 [J4, corresponding author], and IEEE QCE 2025 [C6].
Co-supervised research on surface-code ensemble decoding [C3] and quantum key distribution integrated with classical cryptography and steganography [J2, J3].

posts.title: Agrippan Trilemma: Theoretical Impossibility of Proving Truths
posts.summary: Why it is fundamentally impossible to prove any proposition with absolute certainty, and how Karl Popper's falsifiability allows science to circumvent the three horns of Agrippa's trilemma (infinite regress, circularity, and dogmatic axiom) where religion and metaphysics stall.
posts.content:
It is fundamentally impossible to prove any proposition with absolute certainty. This epistemological problem is known as the **Agrippan Trilemma** (or Münchhausen Trilemma). It arises from a simple logical requirement: any claim to truth must be justified by evidence or logic. However, that justification is itself a claim that requires its own justification. This creates a structural paradox where the foundation of knowledge can never be definitively settled, rendering absolute proof unattainable.

Any attempt to construct a flawless foundation of knowledge will inevitably encounter one of three logical dead ends:

1. **Infinite Regress:** A proposition is justified by a second, the second by a third, and so on indefinitely, without ever reaching a foundational bedrock.
2. **Circular Reasoning:** The chain of justification loops back upon itself, relying on the conclusion to prove the premise.
3. **Dogmatic Assumption (Axiomatic Halting):** The chain of justification is arbitrarily halted by asserting a fundamental premise as an axiom that requires no proof.

---

## Religion, Metaphysics, and Falsifiability

Historically, religion and metaphysics have attempted to resolve this trilemma but ultimately fall victim to its constraints. Religion almost exclusively relies on dogmatic assumption, halting the infinite regress by asserting an absolute endpoint like an infallible deity, divine revelation, or a sacred text. Metaphysics attempts to establish the ultimate nature of reality through pure reason, but it too must eventually rely on unprovable axioms, assuming without tangible evidence that human intuition aligns with the fundamental mechanics of the universe.

Strictly speaking, the scientific method also fails the Agrippan Trilemma: science relies on foundational assumptions such as the uniformity of nature and the reliability of observation. However, science remains our most powerful epistemological tool because of philosopher **Karl Popper's concept of falsifiability**.

Popper argued that science circumvents the trilemma by abandoning the search for absolute proof and instead making specific, risky predictions that can be empirically tested and **proven wrong**. Science does not claim to hold absolute, unassailable truth; rather, it offers the strongest surviving models that have withstood rigorous attempts at refutation.

posts.title: Gödel’s Ontological Argument: Scott’s God and the Case for Tyranny
posts.summary: A formal critique of Dana Scott’s variant of Gödel’s higher-order modal ontological argument (□∃x G(x)): why computational verification in Lean 4 entails modal collapse (p → □p), eliminating alternative possibilities (◇¬p), and why combining modal collapse with retributive punishment renders divine governance tyrannical rather than omnibenevolent.
posts.content:
Proving that a being necessarily exists does not establish that it deserves our admiration. That distinction is central when evaluating Dana Scott’s formulation of Kurt Gödel’s higher-order modal ontological argument.

## 1. Positive Properties and the Formal Gap to Benevolence

Gödel’s argument treats *"positive"* as a technical classification of properties constrained by Scott’s axioms: exactly one of a property and its negation is positive; necessary consequences of positive properties are positive; Godlikeness $G(x)$ (possessing all positive properties) and necessary existence are positive; and positivity persists across possible worlds. From these axioms, the system derives:

$$\Box \exists x \, G(x)$$

Yet calling a formal predicate "positive" does not automatically confer moral goodness. A simple one-world, one-individual countermodel satisfies all of Scott’s axioms while leaving an unconstrained moral predicate $B(x)$ ("$x$ is benevolent") completely unsettled.

## 2. Modal Collapse ($p \to \Box p$) and the Elimination of Alternatives

As verified in computer-checked formalizations in **Lean 4** and **TPTP THF** (Benzmüller & Paleo, 2016; Benzmüller, 2026), Scott’s axioms entail **modal collapse**:

$$p \to \Box p$$

Every true proposition is necessarily true. If $p$ denotes a person committing a wrongful act, $p \to \Box p$ entails $\neg \Diamond \neg p$: there is no accessible possible world in which the agent refrained from the act.

## 3. Why Retribution Under Modal Collapse Is Tyrannical

Let $C$ denote culpability required for basic punitive desert, and $A$ denote having a genuine opportunity to avoid wrongdoing:

- Moral fairness requirement: $C \to A$
- Consequence of modal collapse: $\neg A$
- Therefore: $\neg C$

If a ruler systematically inflicts severe retributive suffering on agents who never possessed an accessible alternative ($\neg \Diamond \neg p$), the punishment lacks the very desert invoked to justify it. Existence alone establishes no entitlement to worship, and a formal proof cannot make an unearned punishment deserved.

posts.title: Beyond Sisyphus: The Limits of Logic at the End of Meaning
posts.summary: An analytical examination of existential meaning, global vs. local accountability, why Albert Camus's command that 'one must imagine Sisyphus happy' commits an is–ought fallacy, and why continuing to live is choosing a non-trivial algebraic structure over the trivial identity group {e}.
posts.content:
I am at a stage in life where *"why"* has superseded *"what"* or *"how."* As an analytical person, I find myself trying to rely less on emotion and more on logic to answer a foundational question: why should we strive in a universe devoid of intrinsic teleology?

## Global Meaninglessness vs. Local Accountability

Under deterministic or Many-Worlds physical frameworks, traditional notions of uncaused agency break down. How then do we justify our actions? The answer lies in separating the **global** from the **local**, much like a software simulation or video game. Globally, outside the confines of the software, no state configuration is objectively "right" or "wrong." Yet locally, within the system's dynamics, an agent cannot evade the causal consequences of its environment.

## The Logical Flaw in Camus's Sisyphus

Albert Camus famously addressed the absurd by declaring that *"one must imagine Sisyphus happy."* While compelling as a poetic coping mechanism, it is logically flawed: Camus transitions abruptly from a **descriptive observation** (the universe has no intrinsic meaning) to a **prescriptive command** (you must rebel and be happy). He brute-forces a subjective aesthetic (the romanticized, defiant rebel) and disguises it as an objective logical conclusion.

We do not need to imagine Sisyphus happy. We can feel compassion for him, or nothing at all; none of these states carry inherent cosmic weight.

## The Trivial Group `{e}` vs. Non-Trivial Structure

Why not simply give up? In abstract algebra and **group theory**, you can always satisfy the group axioms by collapsing a space into the **trivial group** $\{e\}$ containing solely the identity element. It is perfectly consistent, completely stable, and immune to contradiction, yet it contains no structure, no interactions, and yields zero information.

Continuing to live is the **non-trivial group**: complex, asymmetric, and difficult to map. You can always collapse into the trivial identity state, but as an analytical mind, are you sure you don't want to see whether the non-trivial structure holds a symmetry worth discovering?

posts.title: Deriving Lorentz Transformation: Using Linear Algebra
posts.summary: A short derivation of the Lorentz transformation from linear algebra: requiring the light-like lines x = ±ct to stay invariant makes (1, 1) and (1, −1) eigenvectors of the transformation matrix, and demanding T⁻¹(v) = T(−v) fixes γ = 1/√(1 − v²/c²).
posts.content:
To describe an event, both spatial coordinates and time are required simultaneously. For example, we might specify that an event occurred at a certain time in a certain location. In this context, we use a **spacetime diagram** to represent the event geometrically as a point. For the sake of simplicity, we will assume there is only one spatial axis (the $x$-axis) and the time axis. Since time itself is not a physical length, we scale the time axis by defining each unit as $ct$. Here, $c$ is the speed of light in a vacuum.

According to Maxwell's equations and Einstein's special theory of relativity, the speed of light is absolute and constant in a vacuum. Therefore, if an object moves with a uniform velocity $v$, we can write its equation of motion as:

$$x = vt = \frac{v}{c}\,ct = \beta\,ct, \qquad \beta = \frac{v}{c}$$

## Galilean Transformation and Its Failure

Now suppose you are in a reference frame $S$, and your friend is in frame $S'$. The coordinates of your frames are $(x, ct)$ and $(x', ct')$ respectively. Let us assume that at time $t = t' = 0$, the two frames perfectly overlapped, and frame $S'$ is moving with a velocity $v$ along the $+x$-axis relative to frame $S$.

The classical Galilean transformation tells us that:

$$x' = x - vt = x - \beta\,ct, \qquad ct' = ct$$

However, we know that under these transformations, the speed of light would depend on the observer's relative velocity. To preserve the constancy of the speed of light, we assume this relationship must be modified by a factor:

$$x' = \gamma\,(x - \beta\,ct)$$

## Light Rays Must Stay Light Rays

The transformation of the entire spacetime must be linear. Thus, the coordinates must transform according to a matrix equation:

$$\begin{pmatrix} x' \\ ct' \end{pmatrix} = T \begin{pmatrix} x \\ ct \end{pmatrix}$$

Here, $T$ is a transformation matrix that must obey the core postulates of special relativity.

Since the speed of light is constant in both frames, the light-like trajectories $x = ct$ and $x = -ct$ must remain invariant under the transformation $T$. In the language of linear algebra, this means the eigenvectors of matrix $T$ are $\begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix}$ and $\begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix}$.

Based on this, the matrix $T$ must take the following form:

$$T = a \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 \end{pmatrix} + b \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ -1 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix} 1 & -1 \end{pmatrix}$$

Thus $T$ is a symmetric matrix, entirely dependent on the velocity $v$. By comparing terms and substituting, we get:

$$ct' = \gamma\,(-\beta x + ct)$$

## Fixing the Factor $\gamma$

One of the fundamental principles of physics is that the laws of nature are identical in all inertial frames of reference. Therefore, finding the inverse of matrix $T$ is mathematically identical to simply replacing $v$ with $-v$ in the original matrix (because from the perspective of frame $S'$, frame $S$ is just moving at velocity $v$ in the opposite direction along the $-x'$ axis).

Mathematically, this means:

$$T^{-1}(v) = T(-v)$$

When we calculate the inverse and equate it to $T(-v)$, we get:

$$\gamma^2\,(1 - \beta^2) = 1 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \gamma = \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - v^2/c^2}}$$

By plugging $\gamma$ back in, we arrive at the full Lorentz transformation:

$$x' = \frac{x - \beta\,ct}{\sqrt{1 - \beta^2}}, \qquad ct' = \frac{-\beta x + ct}{\sqrt{1 - \beta^2}}$$

## The Geometry of the New Axes

Finally, looking at the axes in the new frame:

- The equation for the $x'$ axis is $ct' = 0$, which simplifies to $ct = \beta x$.
- The equation for the $ct'$ axis is $x' = 0$, which simplifies to $x = \beta\,ct$.

This reveals a profound geometric truth: if an object moves at velocity $v$, its new spacetime axes $x'$ and $ct'$ will rotate inwards, creating an angle of $\tan^{-1}(\beta)$ relative to the original $x$ and $ct$ axes respectively.

posts.title: Trisecting an Angle: With Ruler and Compass
posts.summary: Why an arbitrary angle cannot be trisected with an unmarked straightedge and compass: constructible numbers only reach 2ⁿ-th roots, yet trisection needs the cubic 4x³ − 3x − cos θ = 0. Covers the 60° obstruction, the easy 90° case, and Archimedes' Neusis construction.
posts.content:
Let us talk about an ancient and famous puzzle in geometry today. Is it possible to divide any given angle into three equal parts using only a straightedge (which can only draw straight lines and has no measurement marks) and a compass?

For thousands of years, people tried and failed to trisect an arbitrary angle with just a straightedge and compass. Later, in the 19th century, algebra stepped in to prove that it is indeed impossible! But hidden behind this geometric failure is a brilliant algebraic mystery.

## Constructible Numbers

First, let us understand the geometric limits of a straightedge and compass. Whenever we draw two straight lines with a ruler, or draw circles with a compass to find their intersection points, in the language of algebra, we are actually solving linear equations or, at most, quadratic equations. This means that with a straightedge and compass, we can only create lengths or points through addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and taking square roots. We call these **constructible numbers**.

Why square roots? If the hypotenuse of a right triangle is $x+1$ and one base is $x-1$, the perpendicular height is $\sqrt{(x+1)^2-(x-1)^2}=2\sqrt{x}$. Halving this gives us $\sqrt{x}$. By stacking square roots on top of square roots, we can extract the 4th root, 8th root, or any $2^n$-th root, where $n\in\mathbb{N}=\{0, 1, 2, 3, \dots\}$. But for $2^n = 3$, $n$ is not a natural number, nor is it even a rational number. Therefore, it is impossible to solve any cube root or cubic equation with our geometric toolbox.

## The Cubic Hidden Inside Trigonometry

So, where is the connection between angle trisection and cubic equations? The link lies hidden inside trigonometry.

Suppose we are given an angle $\theta$. Trisecting it means constructing the angle $\theta/3$ geometrically. In the language of coordinate geometry, if we know the value of $\cos\theta$, we need to figure out the value of $\cos(\theta/3)$.

Now, we know:

$$\cos\theta = 4\cos^3(\theta/3) - 3\cos(\theta/3)$$

To make it simpler, if we let $x = \cos(\theta/3)$ and our known angle value $a = \cos\theta$, the above formula takes the form of a beautiful polynomial equation:

$$4x^3 - 3x - a = 0$$

Notice the highest power of $x$ in this equation; this is our coveted cubic equation! This can be easily proven using Euler's famous formula $e^{ix} = \cos x + i\sin x$. When we triple an angle, we are essentially multiplying a number in the complex plane three times in a row. The cubic term is born straight out of the real part of that cubic expansion.

## Why 60° Cannot Be Trisected

Now let us look at a practical example. Suppose we are given a $60^\circ$ angle. We want to divide it into three equal parts to make a $20^\circ$ angle. We know that $\cos 60^\circ = \tfrac{1}{2}$, so our equation becomes:

$$4x^3 - 3x - \tfrac{1}{2} = 0$$

This equation is completely "irreducible" over rational numbers. It cannot be broken down into linear or quadratic equations by any means. To solve it, we must inevitably resort to cube roots. But our compass only knows how to do square roots! Since $3$ is by no means a power of $2$, the geometric scope of a straightedge and compass will never be able to touch the solution to this cubic equation. And this is exactly why trisecting a $60^\circ$ angle using standard rules is impossible.

## The Exceptions

Interestingly, there are exceptions for certain angles! For example, with a $90^\circ$ angle, $\cos 90^\circ = 0$, so the equation becomes:

$$4x^3 - 3x = 0 \quad\text{or}\quad x\,(4x^2 - 3) = 0$$

In other words, the cubic equation breaks down into a linear equation ($x = 0$) and a quadratic equation ($4x^2 - 3 = 0$). That is why trisecting a $90^\circ$ angle into $30^\circ$ with a straightedge and compass is no big deal.

## Changing the Axioms: Archimedes' Neusis

Does this mean angle trisection is entirely impossible? We assumed an unmarked straightedge, a compass, and a flat plane. What if we change these axioms? The Greek mathematician Archimedes showed that by simply placing two marks on the straightedge, it is possible to extract cube roots using a method called **Neusis construction**. Similarly, using the geometric rules of Japanese origami art (Huzita-Hatori axioms), it is perfectly possible to find cube roots and solve any cubic equation just by folding paper!

Let us wrap up today's discussion with Master Archimedes' method.

First, centering at the vertex $O$ of the given $\angle AOD = \theta$, draw an arc of any radius $r$. Let us say this arc intersects the two sides of the angle at points $A$ and $D$ respectively. Extend the bottom side $OD$ straight in the opposite direction (to the left). Now, take a straightedge where the distance between two marked points is exactly equal to our chosen radius $r$. Position the straightedge such that:

- The straightedge passes through point $A$.
- The first mark on the ruler sits exactly on the circumference of the circle (let us call this point $C$).
- The second mark touches the extended line $OD$ (let us call this point $E$).

If we draw the line $AE$ in this position, the $\angle AEC$ formed at the left end of the line will be exactly one-third of the original angle. That means our angle trisection is complete! How is this possible? When the straightedge is simultaneously rotated and slid in the Neusis method, a special high-degree curve is created in geometry, known as the **Conchoid of Nicomedes**. memes.title: The Quantum Choice
memes.description: Bell’s Theorem offering you the ultimate Red Pill / Blue Pill choice: Locality or Realism.
memes.explanation: John Stewart Bell proved in 1964 that any physical theory satisfying both Locality (no superluminal causal influences) and Realism (physical observables possess pre-existing definite values prior to measurement, i.e., local hidden variables) must obey Bell’s inequalities. Because quantum mechanics and loophole-free Bell test experiments violate these inequalities up to the Tsirelson bound 2√2 > 2, nature forces us to give up at least one: Locality or Realism.
memes.desc: Bell’s Theorem offering you the ultimate Red Pill / Blue Pill choice: Locality or Realism.

memes.title: A Higher Plane
memes.description: Normal people: "Everyone is stupid except me." Mathematician: Stereographic projection from the North Pole onto the "Plane of Stupidity."
memes.explanation: Under stereographic projection of the sphere S² onto the flat plane ℝ² (labeled the "plane of stupidity"), rays drawn from the North Pole N ("Me") map every other point A, B, C, D ∈ S² \ {N} ("Everyone else") bijectively onto points A’, B’, C’, D’ on the plane below, whereas the North Pole itself is the unique point at infinity that escapes projection onto the plane.
memes.desc: Normal people: "Everyone is stupid except me." Mathematician: Stereographic projection from the North Pole onto the "Plane of Stupidity."

memes.title: A Victim of Success
memes.description: Fluxonium and 0–π qubits when intrinsic noise resilience makes them hard to measure: "I am a victim of my own success."
memes.explanation: In superconducting circuit QED, protected qubits such as heavy fluxonium and the 0–π qubit achieve long relaxation (T₁) and dephasing (T₂) coherence times by localizing the |0⟩ and |1⟩ wavefunctions in disjoint valleys of phase space with exponentially suppressed transition matrix elements. However, decoupling the qubit from environmental noise channels simultaneously weakens its dipole coupling to external microwave drive lines and dispersive readout resonators, creating a fundamental hardware trade-off between intrinsic noise protection and fast, high-fidelity measurement.
memes.desc: Fluxonium and 0–π qubits when intrinsic noise resilience makes them hard to measure: "I am a victim of my own success."

memes.title: Ground State Urge
memes.description: Midnight urge when I feel low: applying the annihilation operator â = (q̂ + ip̂)/√2 to the ground state |g⟩.
memes.explanation: In the quantum harmonic oscillator, the bosonic annihilation (lowering) operator â = (q̂ + ip̂)/√2 lowers any excited energy eigenstate |n⟩ by one quantum via â|n⟩ = √n|n−1⟩. When the system is already at rock bottom in its ground state |g⟩ ≡ |0⟩, acting with â does not produce a lower energy state; it annihilates the state vector completely into the zero vector: â|g⟩ = 0.
memes.desc: Midnight urge when I feel low: applying the annihilation operator â = (q̂ + ip̂)/√2 to the ground state |g⟩.

memes.title: One Ring to Rule Them All
memes.description: Gandalf: "What can you see?" The One Ring inscribed with (ℤ, +, ·). Frodo: "just a ring."
memes.explanation: When Gandalf pulls the ring from the hearth expecting the fiery Black Speech of Mordor, the glowing inscription instead reads (ℤ, +, ·): the set of integers equipped with standard addition and multiplication, which is the canonical textbook archetype of a commutative ring in abstract algebra. Hence Frodo’s literal algebraic reply: "just a ring."
memes.desc: Gandalf: "What can you see?" The One Ring inscribed with (ℤ, +, ·). Frodo: "just a ring."

memes.title: Inner Product Civil War
memes.description: ⟨x, αy + βz⟩ = α⟨x, y⟩ + β⟨x, z⟩ vs. ⟨αx + βy, z⟩ = α⟨x, z⟩ + β⟨y, z⟩: The eternal Physics vs. Math inner-product civil war.
memes.explanation: On a complex Hilbert space, a sesquilinear inner product must be linear in one argument and conjugate-linear (antilinear) in the other so that ⟨x, x⟩ > 0. Physicists follow Paul Dirac’s bra-ket convention ⟨x | αy + βz⟩ = α⟨x|y⟩ + β⟨x|z⟩ (linear in the second slot, the ket, and conjugate-linear in the first slot, the bra), whereas pure mathematicians define ⟨αx + βy, z⟩ = α⟨x, z⟩ + β⟨y, z⟩ (linear in the first slot).
memes.desc: ⟨x, αy + βz⟩ = α⟨x, y⟩ + β⟨x, z⟩ vs. ⟨αx + βy, z⟩ = α⟨x, z⟩ + β⟨y, z⟩: The eternal Physics vs. Math inner-product civil war.

memes.title: A Subtle Truth in QEC
memes.description: "If a QECC can correct X and Z errors, it may not correct ZX error." Why linearity alone does not automatically guarantee Y-error correction.
memes.explanation: A classic subtlety in Quantum Error Correction (QEC): by the error-discretization theorem, if a QECC corrects an error set E, linearity guarantees it corrects any linear combination αE₁ + βE₂ of operators in E. However, a simultaneous bit-and-phase flip ZX = −iY is a multiplicative matrix product of Z and X, not a linear combination! While CSS codes decode X-type and Z-type syndromes independently (and therefore do correct ZX whenever they correct X and Z), a general QECC whose syndrome space or Knill–Laflamme conditions ⟨ψ_a|E_α† E_β|ψ_b⟩ = C_αβ δ_ab only distinguish {I, X, Z} can have the syndrome of ZX alias with another error, failing to correct ZX.
memes.desc: "If a QECC can correct X and Z errors, it may not correct ZX error." Why linearity alone does not automatically guarantee Y-error correction.

memes.title: A Function or a Distribution?
memes.description: "How about people who call Dirac Delta a function?" "Straight to hell. To the boiler room of hell."
memes.explanation: No pointwise function δ: ℝ → ℝ can vanish everywhere for x ≠ 0 and still have Lebesgue integral ∫_{−∞}^∞ δ(x) dx = 1 (its integral would be identically 0). Rigorously, the Dirac delta δ is not a function at all, but a continuous linear functional (a Schwartz distribution or Radon measure) acting on smooth test functions φ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ) via the evaluation pairing ⟨δ, φ⟩ = φ(0).
memes.desc: "How about people who call Dirac Delta a function?" "Straight to hell. To the boiler room of hell."

memes.title: Statistical Subtlety
memes.description: "If p-value is greater than significance level, you can’t reject the null hypothesis." "So you accept it?" "No."
memes.explanation: In Neyman–Pearson and Fisherian frequentist hypothesis testing, a p-value exceeding the significance threshold α (p > α) only means the observed data lack sufficient statistical power or evidence to reject H₀ ("fail to reject H₀"). Because absence of evidence is not evidence of absence (especially under high Type II error β), failing to reject H₀ never proves that H₀ is true.
memes.desc: "If p-value is greater than significance level, you can’t reject the null hypothesis." "So you accept it?" "No."

memes.title: What is '+'?
memes.description: 1 + 1 = ? When "2" isn’t on the board, and A: 0, B: 1, C: 11, D: 10 are all simultaneously right.
memes.explanation: Every single multiple-choice option is valid in a different algebraic or numeral system: A (1 + 1 = 0) holds in the finite field 𝔽₂ = ℤ/2ℤ (modulo-2 / XOR arithmetic); B (1 + 1 = 1) holds in Boolean algebra (logical OR, 1 ∨ 1 = 1); C (1 + 1 = 11) holds in unary representation or string concatenation ("1" + "1"); and D (1 + 1 = 10) holds in binary (base-2) arithmetic.
memes.desc: 1 + 1 = ? When "2" isn’t on the board, and A: 0, B: 1, C: 11, D: 10 are all simultaneously right.

memes.title: Nowhere Differentiable
memes.description: "Me chilling because I can differentiate any continuous function" vs. Weierstrass’s monster f(x) = ∑ cos(13ⁿπx)/2ⁿ.
memes.explanation: In 1872, Karl Weierstrass shattered 19th-century mathematical intuition by constructing the pathological function f(x) = ∑_{n=0}^∞ cos(13ⁿπx)/2ⁿ. Because the geometric weights 1/2ⁿ converge absolutely by the Weierstrass M-test, f(x) is uniformly continuous everywhere on ℝ; yet because the frequency-amplitude product ab = 13/2 > 1 + 3π/2, its difference quotients oscillate wildly at every scale, making f(x) differentiable nowhere!
memes.desc: "Me chilling because I can differentiate any continuous function" vs. Weierstrass’s monster f(x) = ∑ cos(13ⁿπx)/2ⁿ.

memes.title: The Miracle of Holomorphy
memes.description: f: ℝ → ℝ (C¹ ⇏ C^∞ ⇏ C^ω) vs. f: ℂ → ℂ (C¹ ⇔ C^∞ ⇔ C^ω).
memes.explanation: For real functions f: ℝ → ℝ, being once continuously differentiable (C¹) does not imply smoothness (C^∞), and even being infinitely differentiable (C^∞, such as Cauchy’s flat bump function e^(−1/x²) for x > 0) does not imply analyticity (C^ω, locally equal to a convergent Taylor series). In complex analysis (f: ℂ → ℂ), however, the Cauchy–Riemann equations and Cauchy’s Integral Formula work a miracle: any function that is complex-differentiable just once on an open domain is automatically infinitely differentiable (C^∞) and analytic (C^ω), so C¹ ⇔ C^∞ ⇔ C^ω!
memes.desc: f: ℝ → ℝ (C¹ ⇏ C^∞ ⇏ C^ω) vs. f: ℂ → ℂ (C¹ ⇔ C^∞ ⇔ C^ω).
